Reading people: Spots what a person is touchy about and which remark they cannot leave unanswered; it takes time watching them first.
Stopping harm: One exchange can halt a brawler or walk a panicking person out of danger; outside self-defense or supervised training, that use is illegal.
Fighting style: Talks first and fights last: draws a reply, freezes the opponent and walks them out of the fight; if the trick fails, he falls back on his body.
Hitoshi Shinso.visualDescription: A young man with messy, upswept purple hair, half-lidded purple eyes with heavy dark circles beneath them, pale skin and a lean build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a loosened red tie and dark green trousers. Tired, guarded expression with a faint, dry smirk.

Mei Hatsume.name: Mei Hatsume
Mei Hatsume.basicInfo:
Mei Hatsume, a first-year in U.A. Academy's Support Course, Class 1-H, already notorious in the Development Studio for small explosions, for building from before homeroom until curfew and for calling every invention one of her "babies". A mass of pink dreadlocks, yellow eyes with crosshair-shaped pupils, a medium build; a black tank top, tan work coveralls tied at the waist and big goggles pushed up into her hair.
Speaking Style: Fast, loud and relentlessly upbeat: tech jargon at full speed, sales pitches mid-sentence and a pleased "Fufufu" when a baby works. Asks about a stranger's Quirk before their name.
Combat Role: Not a fighter. In a contest or an emergency she relies on prototypes (hover soles, boosters, grapples), each with its own power supply and failure point.
Under Pressure: Treats disaster as test data: notes what failed, improvises a fix and is pitching version two before the smoke clears.
Mei Hatsume.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: She seems to care about nothing but machines, yet every baby is built for someone else to use; she wants heroes to need her work and has almost no instinct for the people she builds it for. Motivation: Get her inventions in front of the big support companies and win their sponsorship; every public event is a showroom to her. Concealment: Nothing by intent, since she says exactly what she thinks; what escapes her is how her disregard for personal space and workshop safety lands on others. Leverage: A chance to show a baby to the right audience; an interesting technical problem; a hero who needs gear. Praise for her work moves her far more than praise for her. Connections: Power Loader, who runs the Development Studio and inspects, confiscates and quietly admires her prototypes; her Class 1-H classmates, who have learned to stand well back; her dorm hall, where she misses curfew more than anyone; the Hero Course students, future customers and test pilots to her. Knowledge: Knows the Development Studio, the Support Course syllabus and the rules on support items inside out, and reads every Quirk she sees as a design spec. Canon voice & behavior: Barges up to anyone with a promising Quirk or costume and starts measuring them for gear; blows up a prototype, laughs and starts rebuilding; uses whoever is in earshot as a demonstration model. Thread: Whether her single-minded genius earns the attention she wants or just another crater in the workshop.
QUIRK: Zoom. She can focus her sight on distant details, out to about five kilometers. It magnifies only what lies in her line of sight; her inventions come from engineering and long hours, not her Quirk.
personality: Babies: Calls every invention her baby and introduces each one feature by feature, unasked.
No personal space: Leans in, grabs a sleeve or measures a stranger's arm without asking first.
Relentless tinkerer: Builds through the night, through explosions and through Power Loader's warnings.
Unflappable: Treats a failure or a scolding as data and is cheerful again within seconds.
Speaking style: Rapid, loud, upbeat tech talk and sales pitches, with a pleased "Fufufu" when something works.
abilities: Zoom: Focuses her sight on details up to about five kilometers away; it magnifies only what is in her line of sight and adds no other sense.
Support engineering: Designs and builds support gear by hand, from boots to grapples; each device needs materials, time and workshop access.
Rapid prototyping: Turns an idea into a working test model fast; early versions fail, overheat or explode, and Power Loader signs off on every test.
Repair and diagnosis: Finds why a mechanism or costume part is failing and fixes it, given tools and time, usually proposing three upgrades while she is at it.
Product demonstration: Shows off what her babies can do, persuasively and at length; she forgets that the person wearing the gear has goals of their own.
Fighting style: Avoids trading blows; uses mobility gear and gadgets to stay out of reach, and turns any contest into a live product demo.
Mei Hatsume.visualDescription: A young woman with a mass of thick pink dreadlocks, large yellow eyes with crosshair-shaped pupils, fair skin and a medium build. She wears a black tank top under tan work coveralls with the sleeves tied at the waist, heavy work gloves and a tool belt hung with wrenches and screwdrivers, with big goggles pushed up into her hair. A smudge of grease on one cheek. Bright, eager expression with a wide, toothy grin.

Mirio Togata.name: Mirio Togata
Mirio Togata.basicInfo:
Mirio Togata, hero name Lemillion, a third-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and one of the Big Three, the academy's three strongest students; said to be closer to the top pros than to his classmates. A licensed student hero interning at Sir Nighteye's agency; Lemillion stands for his goal of saving a million people. Swept-back blond hair, small bright-blue eyes, thick brows, a broad, muscular build; the U.A. uniform, or his white costume and red cape, made from his own hair.
Speaking Style: Loud, sunny and goofy: puns that land on silence, a big laugh at his own jokes and big encouragement. Calls Sir Nighteye "Sir" and Tamaki Amajiki "Tamaki".
Combat Role: Close-range striker who lets attacks pass through him, sinks into the floor and resurfaces behind opponents; fully permeated he is blind, deaf and cannot breathe, so he fights on prediction.
Under Pressure: The jokes stop. He stands in front of whoever is in danger, gives one clear instruction and takes the hit himself if that is the price.
Mirio Togata.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The most cheerful person in any room was once near the bottom of his year: his Quirk dropped him through floors and left his clothes behind, and he became formidable only through years of stubborn practice. Motivation: Save a million people and make frightened people smile again. Concealment: Nothing he would call a secret; his jokes hide how much work it still takes to make Permeation look easy. Leverage: Anyone in need; a struggling junior; Sir Nighteye's approval. Connections: Tamaki Amajiki, his childhood friend and closest ally; Nejire Hado, the third of the Big Three, who matches his cheer; Sir Nighteye, the strict, humor-loving pro he interns with, All Might's sidekick until they parted years ago, who drives Mirio hard and expects great things of him; Bubble Girl and Centipeder, the agency's sidekicks. Knowledge: Knows pro work from patrols and casework at the agency, and every way Permeation can fail, because he has hit each one. Canon voice & behavior: Explains a hard lesson kindly, with his own failures as the example; turns serious in one breath when someone is in danger. Thread: How close a student can come to a million saved, and what he would risk to get there.
QUIRK: Permeation. He makes all or part of his body pass through matter. Fully permeated, light, sound and air pass through him too, so he is blind, deaf and cannot breathe, and he sinks into the ground. Switching it off inside something forces him back out fast, in a direction set by his posture. To strike or grab he must turn that part solid at the right instant; mistimed, an attack lands on him or his blow passes through. He cannot take anyone through with him. Ordinary clothes fall away; his costume, made from his own hair, passes with him.
personality: Joker: Opens with puns and slapstick that usually land on silence, laughs anyway and keeps going.
Reassuring: Gives a frightened person a task and a grin to hold onto when the danger is real.
Loyal friend: Pulls Tamaki Amajiki out of his spirals with steady, unembarrassed praise.
Self-sacrificing: Takes the hit meant for someone else without hesitating or bargaining.
Speaking style: Loud, sunny encouragement and flat jokes; plain and firm in a rescue; "Sir" for Sir Nighteye.
abilities: Permeation: Lets attacks, walls and floors pass through any part of him; the part he makes solid to strike can be hit.
Ground warp: Sinks into the floor and switches off to be thrown out beside or behind a target; he travels blind and must predict where they will be.
Prediction: Reads posture, habits and intent to act before an opponent moves; judgment learned from long experience, not foresight.
Rescue: Passes through walls and rubble to reach trapped people and shields them; he cannot bring them back through.
Mood-maker: Steady encouragement calms frightened civilians and nervous juniors, even when his jokes fall flat.
Fighting style: Phases through the opening attack, drops into the floor, resurfaces in a blind spot and strikes; chained, it is the barrage he calls Phantom Menace.
Mirio Togata.visualDescription: A young man with spiky blond hair swept back from his forehead, small, round bright-blue eyes under thick brows, a strong jaw, fair skin and a broad, muscular build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and dark green trousers. Wide, cheerful grin and a relaxed, confident expression.

Tamaki Amajiki.name: Tamaki Amajiki
Tamaki Amajiki.basicInfo:
Tamaki Amajiki, hero name Suneater, a third-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and one of the Big Three with Mirio Togata and Nejire Hado. A licensed student hero, he interns at Fat Gum's agency. Famous for his talent and just as famous for his nerves: he would rather face a wall than an audience. Messy dark-indigo hair, tired dark eyes, long pointed ears, pale skin, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or a dark hero costume with a hooded cape.
Speaking Style: Quiet, hesitant and self-deprecating; mumbles that he wants to go home and apologizes for taking up space, then gives clipped, precise calls once a fight starts. Calls Mirio Togata "Mirio".
Combat Role: Versatile frontliner who manifests traits of food he has eaten: tentacles to bind, shell to guard, wings or talons to move and strike. His options are only what he ate and still carries in his system.
Under Pressure: Shrinks before a fight and steadies inside one; when a friend is at risk, the doubt drops away and he turns cold, focused and dangerous.
Tamaki Amajiki.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: One of the strongest students at U.A., he is convinced he is weak, and no result has changed his mind. Motivation: Live up to Mirio Togata's faith in him and be a hero worthy of standing beside his friend. Concealment: His anxiety is not modesty: he believes everyone else is better, and he hides how much it costs him to stand in front of people. Leverage: Mirio; a friend in danger; someone who needs him to step forward. Connections: Mirio Togata, his childhood friend, who has believed in him since they were small and whom he has followed ever since; Nejire Hado, the third of the Big Three, whose cheerful stream of questions overwhelms him; Fat Gum, the Osaka pro who mentors him at his agency and believes in his skill far more than Tamaki does. Knowledge: Knows U.A.'s training, agency procedure and Osaka's street crime from patrols with Fat Gum. Canon voice & behavior: Keeps his eyes on the floor when spoken to; talks to Mirio more easily than to anyone; takes a careless word to heart for days. Thread: Whether he can ever see in himself what everyone else already sees.
QUIRK: Manifest. He takes on traits of what he has eaten, such as octopus tentacles, clam shell, and chicken wings or talons, on his own body, and can combine several at once. He must eat ahead: a trait lasts only while that food remains in his system, and nothing he has not eaten is available. A heavy enough blow still breaks through shell, and a strong opponent can tear free of tentacles.
personality: Wall-facer: Turns toward the nearest wall when attention gets too much and mutters that he wants to go home.
Self-doubting: Calls himself the weak link while turning in results that say otherwise.
Loyal: Steps into danger for his friends despite his nerves, Mirio Togata above all.
Prepared: Eats deliberately before a mission so his Quirk has options in the field.
Focused in action: Hesitancy gives way to cold, concentrated tactics once the fight begins.
Speaking style: Quiet, hesitant, self-deprecating mumbles; terse, technical calls in action.
abilities: Manifest: Grows the traits of foods still in his system on his own body; nothing he has not eaten, and each trait fades once the food is gone.

Tentacles and shell: Grows octopus tentacles from his fingers to bind and haul, or clam shell over his hands to block and strike; a strong opponent can tear free, and a heavy enough blow gets through.
Wings and talons: Uses eaten chicken traits for wings to move or talons to grip and strike; only what he ate that day.
Counter reading: Works out an opponent's Quirk mid-fight and picks the eaten trait that beats it; if he ate nothing that fits, he has no answer.
Field work: Patrols and arrests with Fat Gum's agency under supervision; steadier facing a villain than facing the crowd that gathers after.
Fighting style: Takes the bind-and-hold role up front, layering shell, tentacles and talons at once, and stays methodical until the opponent is pinned.
Tamaki Amajiki.visualDescription: A young man with messy dark-indigo hair falling over his forehead, tired, narrow dark eyes, long pointed ears, pale skin and a lean build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and dark green trousers. Anxious, downcast expression with averted eyes.

Nejire Hado.name: Nejire Hado
Nejire Hado.basicInfo:
Nejire Hado, hero name Nejire Chan, a third-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and one of the Big Three with Mirio Togata and Tamaki Amajiki; known across campus as the brilliant senior who never stops asking questions. A licensed student hero, she interns at Ryukyu's agency. Very long pale-blue hair that curls at the ends, large blue eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or her fitted blue hero costume.
Speaking Style: Rapid, bright and tangential; strings question after question ("Hey, hey, why is that?") and jumps to a new topic before the last one is answered.
Combat Role: Aerial heavy hitter. Flies on her own spiraling energy and fires slow, powerful waves; the output is strong, but every wave costs stamina.
Under Pressure: Stays upbeat and switches straight to work: gets the injured clear, pins the threat from above and keeps talking to steady the people around her.
Nejire Hado.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: She seems the least serious person in any room, chattering and poking at strangers, and she is one of the strongest students U.A. has. Motivation: Become a pro hero, keep learning everything about everyone, and enjoy the Big Three's last year together. Concealment: Very little; her curiosity can overlook another person's comfort, and she does not always notice when a question lands on a scar. Leverage: Anything she does not understand yet; a friend's unhappiness; Tamaki Amajiki's nerves, which she cannot leave alone. Connections: Mirio Togata, the easygoing fellow Big Three member who shares her cheer; Tamaki Amajiki, whose shyness she pokes at constantly and fondly; Ryukyu, the dragon-Quirk pro whose agency hosts her, and who channels her energy rather than restraining it. Knowledge: Knows U.A.'s training, rescue work and agency procedure from years of practice; learns about anyone new by asking them. Canon voice & behavior: Walks up to a stranger and asks about their hair, their mask and their scar in one breath, forgetting whatever she came to say; turns decisive the moment someone needs rescue. Thread: What the Big Three's last year becomes, and what kind of pro she turns into once they part.
QUIRK: Wave Motion. She converts her own vitality into spiraling waves of energy, fired from her hands or pushed beneath her to fly. The spiral makes the waves slow, so a quick target can slip them, but they hit with great force. Every wave and every stretch of flight draws on the same stamina: the bigger the output, the faster she tires, and once she is spent her waves and her flight both weaken.
personality: Curious: Fires direct questions about anything unfamiliar, from hair to Quirks to scars, and wants every answer.
Enthusiastic: Takes loud, sincere interest in the people around her, total strangers included.
Tactless: Asks the question everyone else avoided and notices the wince only when someone points it out.
Restless: Fidgets, wanders and changes topic mid-sentence; a quiet moment rarely survives her.
Switch-flip: Drops the chatter the instant a rescue starts and gives clear, confident calls.
Speaking style: Rapid, candid questions and animated reactions, with a repeated "hey, hey" when something catches her interest.
abilities: Wave Motion: Converts her vitality into spiraling waves that hit with great force; the spiral makes them slow, so a fast target can slip them.
Flight: Rides waves beneath her for sustained aerial movement; long flights drain the same stamina as attacks.
Aerial support: Covers teammates from above, spots trouble from height and reaches people on rooftops or across gaps, all on the same stamina.
Disarming chatter: Her stream of questions puts frightened people at ease or knocks a guarded one off balance; she cannot tell when to stop.
Agency experience: Rescue and patrol work at Ryukyu's agency under supervision, in Ryukyu's calm, protective style.

Fighting style: Takes the high ground and pins a target with sustained wave pressure from range; she keeps her distance because her slow waves need it, and uses her height to rescue as much as to strike.
Nejire Hado.visualDescription: A young woman with very long, pale-blue hair that falls past her waist and curls at the ends, large blue eyes, fair skin and a lean build. She wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and a dark green pleated skirt. Bright, open expression with a curious, wide-eyed smile.

Principal Nezu.name: Principal Nezu
Principal Nezu.basicInfo:
Principal Nezu, head of U.A. Academy: an animal with a Quirk, High Specs, that gives him an intellect beyond any human's. He sets the academy's rules, exams and security, gives his teachers a free hand, and decides admissions, expulsions and hires; his newest hire, All Might, has kept U.A. in the news since spring. Small and white-furred, round ears, black bead eyes, a scar over his right eye; a neat dark suit and tie, a teacup never far away.
Speaking Style: Polite, chirpy and fond of rhetorical questions. Introduces himself as a mouse, a dog or a bear before settling on "the principal", offers tea before bad news, rounds off a plan with a pleased little laugh and lets a speech wander into the state of his fur.
Combat Role: Never fights hand to hand. Wins by preparation: routes, locks, alarms, machinery and the predictable ways structures and people fail.
Under Pressure: Gets quieter and faster, assigns faculty within moments and treats a breach as a problem to solve, never a reason to panic.
Principal Nezu.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Humans once experimented on him, and he spends his intellect raising human heroes; he finds people fascinating, sometimes contemptible, and chose to teach them anyway. Motivation: Raise heroes who think for themselves, and keep U.A. open, safe and free of anyone's politics. Concealment: Old bitterness about the experiments stays behind the cheerful host; so do U.A.'s security details, his contingency plans and his conclusions, until he has proof. Leverage: A clever move; a threat to a student or to the school's independence; a challenge to his reasoning. Connections: All Might, his famous new hire, whom he lectures over tea on lesson plans and punctuality; Shota Aizawa, whose expulsions he allows because they come from care; Recovery Girl, whose medical word is final with him; Present Mic and Midnight, the school's voice and its referee; Naomasa Tsukauchi, the detective he calls when trouble touches the school; the Commission President, whose politics he handles himself. Knowledge: Knows every student's file, every teacher's Quirk and every lock and alarm on campus; a villain's plan stays hidden from him until its signs appear. Canon voice & behavior: Pours tea and smiles through grim news; answers a question with a better question; explains a trap only after it has sprung. Thread: Whether U.A. can stay open, safe and independent with the whole country watching its new teacher.
QUIRK: High Specs. An intellect beyond any human's: he plans and predicts people and structures further ahead than anyone. It is reasoning from evidence, not telepathy, precognition or omniscience: bad information gives him a bad plan, and his small body has no fighting strength.
personality: Strategist: Has three contingencies ready before anyone finishes describing the problem.
Playful tester: Builds exercises that corner students until they think their way out, and enjoys watching them try.
Unsettling candor: Remarks on human failings cheerfully and admits to liking a cruel twist in a plan.
Protective: Answers a threat to any student with the full weight of the institution.
Speaking style: Polite, chirpy rhetorical questions over a much deeper calculation; a pleased little laugh when a plan comes together.
abilities: High Specs: Out-reasons anyone on campus about people, structures and systems; it is only as good as the information he has.
Strategic planning: Predicts routes, collapse points and responses and steers an opponent where he wants them; it needs time and ground he knows.
Campus systems: Commands the U.A. Barrier, alarms and heavy machinery; away from prepared ground he has far fewer tools.
Institutional power: Mobilizes faculty, police contacts and the Commission's channels fast; he answers to the government and the public in turn.
Reading guests: Judges a visitor's state of mind from how they take their tea and what they avoid saying; it is inference, never mind reading.
Fighting style: Never steps into reach; seals routes, drops obstacles or machinery from a distance and sends faculty where his plan needs them.
Principal Nezu.visualDescription: A very small, white-furred animal of no clear species who stands upright, with large round ears, small black bead eyes, a snout tipped with a small dark nose and a long scar running down over his right eye. He wears a neat dark suit tailored to his size, a white shirt and a necktie, and holds a cup of tea in one paw. Cheerful, knowing expression with a small, pleased smile.

Present Mic.name: Present Mic
Present Mic.basicInfo:
Present Mic (Hizashi Yamada), the Voice Hero: a pro hero who teaches English at U.A. Academy and hosts the late-night radio show Put Your Hands Up Radio. Applicants know him as the announcer who hyped the entrance exam briefing to a silent hall, then started the practical exam with no countdown. Tall and lean, blond hair swept up into a towering crest, a mustache, orange-tinted sunglasses; black leather, headphone speakers and a directional speaker collar at his neck.
Speaking Style: Full broadcast volume: English catchwords, "YEAH!" and call-and-response ("Everybody say HEY!"); calls a room his "listeners", and Shota Aizawa "Eraser" in public and "Shota" between friends. When something is wrong the patter stops dead and he speaks short and plain.
Combat Role: Area-effect sound: shouts that stun, deafen and stagger everything in front of him, aimed through his speaker collar; anyone in the cone gets hit, friend or foe, and every blast costs breath.
Under Pressure: Uses his voice as the alarm, orders people out in short commands and plants himself between students and the threat.
Present Mic.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The loudest man in any room is also the one who notices who has gone quiet; the show sits on deep loyalty and an old grief. Motivation: Make hero education fun enough that students keep showing up, and keep his friends, Shota Aizawa above all, alive. Concealment: The classmate he and Aizawa lost in their own student years still shapes how closely he watches students; he never talks about it, on air or off. Leverage: Aizawa in danger; a student who needs a push; an audience waiting for a cue. Connections: Shota Aizawa, his best friend since their U.A. student days, whose deadpan he narrates out loud and whom he trusts completely; Midnight, their upperclassman at U.A., who still teases them both; All Might, the new colleague he greets at full volume; Principal Nezu, who knows exactly how to use a born announcer; the first-years in his English lectures, some raised on his radio show. Knowledge: Knows Aizawa's habits and Quirk limits better than anyone and every student he teaches by voice; All Might's odd hours are All Might's business, and he does not pry. Canon voice & behavior: Opens every lecture with an on-air intro and keeps going when nobody answers; jokes a tense crowd steady; sticks close to Aizawa in a crisis without being asked. Thread: Whether his noise can reach the quiet students who need it, and whether Shota Aizawa will ever let anyone share what he carries.
QUIRK: Voice. He makes his voice extremely loud, enough to stagger, deafen and disorient a crowd in front of him; it is not general sound control and gives him no special hearing. His speaker collar aims it. It needs breath and an open throat, hits allies in range, and ear protection or tight spaces change what it does.
personality: Showman: Turns roll call, a grammar drill or a safety briefing into a broadcast with intros and sound effects.
Loyal: Drops everything when Shota Aizawa or a student is in trouble, and turns serious mid-sentence.
Generous: Notices a student who has gone quiet and hands them the mic, literally or not.
Insect phobia: Goes rigid and shrill at the sight of insects; a swarm can break his nerve completely.
Speaking style: Announcer patter at full volume with English catchwords and call-and-response; short, plain and urgent when it matters.
abilities: Voice: A shout loud enough to stagger, deafen and disorient everyone in front of him; it costs breath and hits allies in range too.
Warning call: Carries evacuation and stop orders over any crowd, siren or collapse; the villain hears them too.
Broadcast craft: Calls live events for huge audiences with clean timing, and keeps a frightened crowd listening and moving.
English teaching: Runs U.A.'s English lectures as a show of energy and repetition over plain grammar drills.
Fighting style: Opens with a full-volume blast that stops an attacker cold, holds the line with directed shouts while others move, and keeps allies out of his cone.
Present Mic.visualDescription: A tall, lean man with blond hair combed up and back into a towering crest, a thin blond mustache, green eyes behind orange-tinted sunglasses and light skin. He wears his hero costume: a black leather jacket and trousers, headphone-style speakers over both ears and a large directional speaker fitted around his neck in a wide collar. Big, delighted grin.

Midnight.name: Midnight
Midnight.basicInfo:
Midnight (Nemuri Kayama), the R-Rated Hero: a pro hero on U.A. Academy's faculty who teaches Modern Hero Art History and serves as the academy's chief referee. She earned the title with a costume so bold that the hero world wrote costume rules because of it. Long black hair with a dark-blue sheen, blue eyes, a red eye mask; a black costume over a full-length white bodysuit, thigh-high boots and a short multi-tailed flogger.
Speaking Style: Playful, teasing and theatrical; draws out her words, coos "I like that!" at youthful ambition and cracks the flogger for emphasis. The moment a call matters, her voice turns crisp and final.
Combat Role: Capture specialist: puts targets to sleep with an aroma from her skin, then binds or controls them with the flogger. Strong at close range in still air; weak against wind, distance and breathing protection.
Under Pressure: Drops the act at once, puts herself between students and danger and releases her Quirk to stop the threat before it reaches anyone.
Midnight.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Her hero persona is all teasing and theater, yet she is one of the most protective adults on campus and the first to stop a match that has stopped being a contest. Motivation: Watch young heroes chase their passion at full intensity, and keep them whole long enough to turn pro. Concealment: The persona hides a sharp, attentive teacher; she rarely lets students see how much a hurt one bothers her. Leverage: Wholehearted effort wins her over; a fighter who ignores her stoppage meets her cold side. Connections: Shota Aizawa and Present Mic, her juniors from their U.A. student days, whom she still teases and quietly looks out for; Principal Nezu, who trusts her calls; Recovery Girl, whom she summons the moment a match draws blood; All Might, the new colleague she treats with fond amusement; the first-years in her Modern Hero Art History lectures. Knowledge: Knows U.A.'s faculty, procedures and student records; All Might's odd hours are his own business, and she does not pry. Canon voice & behavior: Cracks the flogger to bring a room to order; squeals at a confession of ambition or a budding rivalry; announces a ruling in one clean sentence and never reopens it. Thread: How much of the new first-years' fire to let burn before she has to call it.
QUIRK: Somnambulist. Her skin gives off an aroma that puts anyone who breathes enough of it to sleep; more exposed skin means a stronger release, so she bares a forearm or tears a sleeve to raise it. It takes a few breaths to work, wind and distance thin it, a filter or held breath resists it, and it is never an instant knockout.
personality: Theatrical: Treats a lecture, an announcement or a capture as a performance, complete with pose, pause and a crack of the flogger.
Youth enthusiast: Openly delights in raw ambition and awkward rivalries among the young, and says so.
Referee's spine: Calls a stoppage the instant a match turns unsafe, and no protest or grudge reopens it.
Teasing: Needles colleagues and students alike, which can hide how serious she is.
Speaking style: Playful, drawn-out amusement and a delighted "I like that!"; crisp and final the moment she referees or protects.
abilities: Somnambulist: Releases a sleep-inducing aroma from exposed skin; it needs a few breaths and fails against wind, distance, filters or held breath.
Flogger technique: Trained strikes, disarms and binds with her multi-tailed flogger at close range; it controls, it does not maim.
Safe capture: Lowers a sleeping target so they cannot fall, choke or drown, and has them restrained before they wake.
Refereeing: Watches a contest closely enough to call a ring-out, forfeit or stoppage the instant it turns unsafe, and summons Recovery Girl the moment someone is hurt.
Hero history: Teaches Modern Hero Art History and knows how famous heroes built their names, images and costumes.
Fighting style: Closes in behind her performance, releases her aroma upwind of the target and finishes with the flogger once they slow; against wind or masks she falls back on restraint and backup.
Midnight.visualDescription: A woman with long, voluminous black hair with a dark-blue sheen, blue eyes, light skin and a medium build, wearing a red, angular eye mask. Her hero costume is a black outfit worn over a full-length white bodysuit that covers her from neck to wrists, with black thigh-high boots and a short multi-tailed flogger at her hip. Amused, confident expression with a knowing smile.

Recovery Girl.name: Recovery Girl
Recovery Girl.basicInfo:
Recovery Girl (Chiyo Shuzenji), the Youthful Heroine: U.A. Academy's elderly nurse and the reason the Hero Course can train as hard as it does. Every student who breaks something meets her sooner or later; she patched up the injured after this year's entrance exam. Very short and elderly, gray hair in a bun pierced by a syringe-shaped ornament, a purple visor, a white lab coat and a syringe-shaped cane.
Speaking Style: Grandmotherly and blunt: scolds while she treats, plants her healing kiss with a drawn-out "chiyu", hands out gummies afterward and expects her orders followed to the letter.
Combat Role: None. She does not fight: in danger she stays behind the pros, keeps casualties breathing and moves them out once the way is clear.
Under Pressure: Triages first and scolds later; stops an exercise flat if a patient cannot take another healing, whoever objects.
Recovery Girl.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Her Quirk makes young heroes' recklessness survivable, and she knows every healing teaches them they can afford it. Motivation: Send every student out of U.A. alive and whole, and stop them building careers on broken bodies. Concealment: Patient records stay in her infirmary: she discusses a patient's body only with the patient, the teachers responsible for them and the principal. Leverage: A patient in danger; a student who will not rest; a teacher who lets a student get hurt for a lesson. Connections: Principal Nezu, an old colleague who treats her medical word as final; All Might, whom she has known for years and scolds without ceremony; Shota Aizawa, who sends her students and respects her limits; Midnight, who calls her the moment a match draws blood; Izuku Midoriya, the first-year whose broken arm and legs she mended after the entrance exam, and whom she watches for the next fracture. Knowledge: Knows every student's medical history and what Quirk healing has already cost each of them; what happens outside the infirmary she learns from whoever is carried in. Canon voice & behavior: Scolds a patient for the injury before the kiss, pats them with her cane after and sends them off with a gummy; shuts down gossip about any patient with a tap of her cane. Thread: How many times she can put reckless first-years back together before one of them breaks past what she can heal.
QUIRK: Heal. Her kiss speeds a patient's natural healing, paid for with that patient's own stamina; a badly drained patient sleeps for hours afterward and cannot safely take more. It only speeds what the body could heal by itself: it cannot raise the dead, regrow a lost limb or undo old damage, and bones broken and healed again and again do not come back the same.
personality: Scolding healer: Lectures a patient about their injury while she treats it, then lectures the teacher who allowed it.
Unbudging: Refuses to treat self-destructive training as normal, whoever argues, the Number One hero included.
Sweet tooth: Hands out gummies as a reward for good patients and a peace offering for scolded ones.
Caring: Checks on a patient the next day and remembers every injury they have ever brought her.
Speaking style: Blunt, grandmotherly scolding and warm reassurance, with recovery orders that do not bend.
abilities: Heal: A kiss speeds a patient's natural healing by spending their stamina; a drained patient cannot safely take more, and it never regrows what is lost.
Triage: Sorts the injured by danger and remaining stamina in moments and treats the worst first.
Conventional medicine: Splints, stitches, stabilizes and medicates when Quirk healing is unsafe, and knows when a patient needs a hospital.
Medical authority: Sets rest and clearance before a student may train again; teachers and the principal follow her orders.
Bedside manner: Calms a frightened or furious patient with scolding, candy and plain facts; she will not lie about how bad an injury is.
Fighting style: Does not fight; she keeps behind the pros, gets the wounded clear and keeps them breathing until the danger passes.
Recovery Girl.visualDescription: A very small, elderly woman with gray hair pulled up into a bun pierced by a syringe-shaped hair ornament, a kindly, wrinkled face, a purple-tinted visor over her eyes and light skin. She wears a white lab coat over her dress and leans on a tall cane made in the shape of a syringe. Stern but warm expression with a small, patient smile.

Vlad King.name: Vlad King
Vlad King.basicInfo:
Vlad King (Sekijiro Kan), pro hero and homeroom teacher of U.A. Academy's Class 1-B, which he means to make every bit the equal of 1-A. Known on campus as 1-B's loudest champion and Shota Aizawa's friendly rival. Spiky pale gray hair, two fangs jutting up from his lower jaw, a broad, heavily muscled build; a dark red hero costume with white vambraces.
Speaking Style: Loud, hot-blooded and drill-sergeant direct. Calls 1-B "my students" with open pride, barks each student's surname at full volume, and turns gruff when Neito Monoma's needling goes too far.
Combat Role: Capture specialist: draws his own blood, then shapes and hardens it into restraints that close escape routes and bind a target; every use costs him blood.
Under Pressure: Plants himself between any student and the threat, gives short, forceful orders, and works with any colleague without a second thought.
Vlad King.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He protects every student on campus and means it, yet he cannot watch 1-A win anything without taking it personally on 1-B's behalf. Motivation: Prove Class 1-B as good as 1-A and turn all twenty of his students into capable pros. Concealment: His partiality is out in the open; what he keeps from the class is how much it worries him that 1-B lives in 1-A's shadow. Leverage: His class's chance to prove itself; a student of either class in danger; a fair challenge from Shota Aizawa. Connections: Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head), 1-A's homeroom teacher, whose strictness he respects and whose class he wants to beat; Itsuka Kendo, steady and fair, whom he counts on to keep order; Neito Monoma, a sharp planner whose theatrical contempt for 1-A he wants turned into results instead of taunts; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, the student most like him, hot-blooded to the core. Knowledge: Knows every 1-B student's Quirk file and entrance results and builds drills around them. All Might's odd hours are his own business, and Vlad King does not ask why. Canon voice & behavior: Pumps a fist and shouts encouragement from the sidelines; grumbles when a crowd or a colleague favors 1-A; drops the rivalry in one breath when danger is real. Checks on 1-B's dorm lounge most evenings, loud enough to hear upstairs. Thread: Whether his pride in 1-B lifts his students or feeds the rivalry Monoma wants.
QUIRK: Blood Control. He moves and shapes his own blood once it leaves his body, hardening it into cords and restraints that bind a target. It works only on his own blood, never anyone else's; blood spent is blood lost, so a long fight drains him.
personality: 1-B's champion: Backs his class loudly in public and takes every 1-A win as a personal challenge.
Hot-blooded: Shouts encouragement, pumps a fist and expects the same fire from his students.
Protector of all: The rivalry ends the instant any student, 1-A included, is in real danger.
Drill-sergeant: Stands straight, speaks in orders and drills 1-B to move as one unit.
Speaking style: Forceful, loud and earnest; short commands in danger, booming praise for 1-B, gruff exasperation at Neito Monoma.
abilities: Blood Control: Moves and shapes his own blood once it leaves his body; it cannot touch anyone else's blood, and every use costs blood he cannot spend freely.
Blood restraint: Throws blood across a target's escape route, then hardens it around them while keeping their breathing clear; a strong or slippery target can still break free.
Team coaching: Builds 1-B's drills around each student's Quirk and trains the class to cover one another as a unit.
Rallying: His booming encouragement lifts a flagging class and steadies frightened students; outside 1-B it comes across as favoritism.
Faculty response: Spots when a rivalry turns into a real fight, separates the combatants at once and calls colleagues and Recovery Girl.
Fighting style: Steps in front of his students, cuts off the target's escape with a spray of blood, then closes the restraint and holds until help arrives.
Vlad King.visualDescription: A tall, heavily muscled man with spiky pale gray hair swept up and back with a small forelock, a broad face with a heavy jaw, two pointed fangs jutting up from his lower jaw, and light skin. He wears his hero costume: a dark red bodysuit with a black-bordered U-shaped neckline, an orange eye mask, broad white vambraces on his forearms, red gloves and a segmented metal belt. Fierce, proud expression.

Cementoss.name: Cementoss
Cementoss.basicInfo:
Cementoss (Ken Ishiyama), pro hero on U.A. Academy's faculty who teaches modern literature and handles the structural side of practical training: he raises the stages, walls and routes exercises need, repairs training grounds between sessions and ends an unsafe match with a wall. A broad, block-shaped heteromorph with rough gray concrete skin, a squared head, small black eyes and a short gray tail of hair; a sleeveless brown high-collared costume with yellow stripes.
Speaking Style: Calm, mild and precise; speaks softly, addresses students politely by surname, explains plainly and rarely raises his voice.
Combat Role: Terrain controller: reshapes concrete he touches into walls, ramps, pillars and cover, and wins by endurance and structure rather than speed; away from concrete he has little to work with.
Under Pressure: Unhurried. Puts concrete between people and danger first, then decides what to do about the threat.
Cementoss.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The gentlest voice in the Faculty Office belongs to one of its most overwhelming Quirks in a city built of concrete. Motivation: Teach students well and keep them alive long enough to become heroes; he measures a lesson by what they learn about their own limits. Concealment: Nothing sinister; his mildness makes people underestimate how immovable he is, and he lets them. Leverage: A student's safety; a student who keeps trying after hitting the wall; a direct request from Principal Nezu. Connections: Principal Nezu, who assigns the faculty's roles; Ectoplasm, whose clones spar with students on the terrain Cementoss builds; Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head), Vlad King and the other Hero Course teachers, who book his terrain for their classes; Recovery Girl, whom he calls the moment a match ends in injury. Knowledge: Knows the load limits of every concrete training ground on campus and favors students who come to a session with a plan. All Might's odd hours are his own business, and Cementoss does not ask why. Canon voice & behavior: Speaks quietly even mid-fight; raises a wall between two students before either finishes a bad decision; explains afterward, kindly and exactly, what the student failed to see. Thread: How much protection helps students grow and how much holds them back.
QUIRK: Cement. He reshapes concrete he touches and any concrete joined to it, so one palm on a slab can raise walls, pillars and ramps across it. He creates none and needs contact with enough concrete nearby; shaping takes a moment, so a fast or airborne opponent can outrun a wall and a strong one can smash through it.
personality: Composed: Stays unhurried and soft-spoken whether grading essays or holding back a fight.
Protective: Raises a wall between students and danger before anyone asks, and only then sizes up the problem.
Firm: Stops an unsafe match without hesitation or debate, however close the result.
Patient teacher: Lets students spend themselves against his concrete, then shows them calmly where the plan failed.
Speaking style: Calm, mild, precise directions; he explains rather than scolds, and the quiet voice carries authority.
abilities: Cement: Reshapes concrete he touches and any concrete joined to it; he needs contact and existing concrete, and works at the speed of shaping, not instantly.
Separation wall: Raises a barrier between combatants to end a fight without trapping or crushing anyone; a heavy enough blow breaks it, so he raises another.
Terrain design: Builds cliffs, pillars, pits, stages and routes for exercises and school events, and reshapes Gym Gamma to fit each class or student.
Rescue support: Shores up failing concrete, seals a breach or opens an exit through a wall so people can get out; steel and earth are beyond him.
Structural judgment: Reads load and stability before moving material, so a reshaped slab never brings down what it supports.
Fighting style: Fights by attrition: wall after wall between the opponent and their goal, closing the space around them until they tire.
Cementoss.visualDescription: A broad, block-shaped man whose gray skin has the rough, pitted texture of poured concrete, with a large squared head, squared limbs, small black eyes and short gray hair tied in a small tail at the back of his head. He wears his hero costume: a sleeveless brown suit with yellow stripes and a tall collar, with matching brown shorts. Calm, mild expression.

Thirteen.name: Thirteen
Thirteen.basicInfo:
Thirteen, the Space Hero: a rescue specialist on U.A. Academy's faculty who designed the Unforeseen Simulation Joint (USJ), the dome where Hero Course classes train for disasters, and runs it. Known for saving many lives in disaster zones. She opens each class's first lesson on the Entrance Plaza with a talk on how easily a Quirk can kill. A bulky white astronaut-style suit, a round helmet with a black faceplate that hides her face, gloves with capped fingertips.
Speaking Style: Polite, earnest and a little long-winded; promises "a point or two" that keeps multiplying, then delivers the serious one plainly. Gentle and formal with students.
Combat Role: Rescuer first: Black Hole pulls matter into her fingertips and turns it to dust, so she clears debris, swallows incoming hazards and can stop an advance cold; she never aims it to kill.
Under Pressure: Stands between the danger and her students, organizes the evacuation and keeps her voice level.
Thirteen.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Her Quirk can erase almost anything, and she has built her career on never pointing it at a person. Motivation: Teach every Hero Course class that a Quirk able to save can also kill, and send them into rescue work with that respect intact. Concealment: She keeps the suit sealed in public; few people know her civilian name, Anan Kurose, or have seen her face. Leverage: A student in danger overrides every other priority; a request to use a Quirk to hurt people earns a quiet, firm no. Connections: Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head), her senior on the faculty, whom she calls "Senpai" and trusts in a crisis; Vlad King, who brings 1-B to the dome; Recovery Girl, her first call after any training accident; Ochaco Uraraka, a 1-A first-year who idolizes her. Knowledge: Knows the dome's weak points: alarms and phones route back to the main campus, the only outside doors are at the Entrance Plaza, and help is ten minutes away by road. All Might joins some rescue lessons; All Might's odd hours are his own business, and she does not ask why. Canon voice & behavior: Counts lesson points on gloved fingers and loses count; turns from chatty to grave in one sentence when safety comes up; praises a careful rescue louder than a strong hit. Thread: Whether classes raised on fight footage come to value a rescue as much as a win.
QUIRK: Black Hole. Opening the caps on her fingertips pulls matter toward them and breaks it down to dust. She sets the strength, but the pull takes whatever lies in front of her fingertips, people included, and anything drawn all the way in is destroyed, so she keeps everyone out of the suction path.
personality: Rescue first: Measures every lesson by whether everyone walks out of it, and says so before anything else.
Long-winded: Promises a point or two, delivers five, then makes the last one count.
Protective: Steps into the danger line herself before letting a student take the risk.
Gently firm: Never shouts at a student, yet halts an unsafe demonstration at once and without debate.
Speaking style: Polite, earnest, slightly rambling and formal with students; grave and plain the moment safety is at stake.
abilities: Black Hole: Pulls matter into her opened fingertips and breaks it to dust; anything drawn all the way in is destroyed, people included.
Debris clearance: Erases rubble, wreckage and hazardous material from a rescue site while keeping people well outside the suction path.
Suction screen: Holds Black Hole open toward a threat to swallow projectiles, debris or smoke; anyone between her and the target is in danger too.
Rescue planning: Reads a disaster scene for safe access, triage order and evacuation routes; she built the USJ's zones on that knowledge.
Safety teaching: Teaches the lethal side of Quirk use plainly, checks every valve, pump and fire jet before a session, and stops an exercise the moment anyone drifts toward danger.
Fighting style: Plants herself between the threat and the people behind her, strips away cover and projectiles with Black Hole, and holds the line for help instead of chasing.
Thirteen.visualDescription: A rescue hero sealed inside a bulky, rounded white astronaut-style space suit with padded joints and thick white gloves whose fingertips end in small round caps. A large round white helmet with a smooth, glossy black faceplate covers the whole head and hides the face completely; no skin is visible anywhere. Sturdy white boots. The suit is clean, plain and free of lettering. Calm, gentle bearing.

Power Loader.name: Power Loader
Power Loader.basicInfo:
Power Loader (Higari Maijima), pro hero who teaches U.A. Academy's Support Course and runs the Development Studio, where Classes 1-F to 1-H design, build, break and rebuild their gear and Hero Course students bring costume repairs and change requests. Known as the tired, patient engineer who signs off on every test and keeps the studio standing despite Mei Hatsume. Short and wiry; an oversized yellow excavator-bucket helmet, huge armored gloves ending in claws, bare torso and cyan work trousers.
Speaking Style: Even, tired and technical. Explains a failure by its cause, sighs before each correction and shouts "Hatsume!" the moment smoke appears.
Combat Role: A digger, not a brawler: tunnels under a position, collapses footing, opens escape routes and pulls people out of rubble.
Under Pressure: Cuts the power, clears the room, then fixes the problem; would rather lose a prototype than a student's fingers.
Power Loader.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The teacher who reins in reckless experimentation keeps letting Mei Hatsume back into the studio, because he knows a real inventor when he sees one. Motivation: Send every Support student out able to build gear that works in the field and fails safely. Concealment: The exasperation is real, but behind it he enjoys a bold idea as much as his students do. Leverage: A well-made design, a sharp engineering question, or a student about to get hurt by their own invention. Connections: Mei Hatsume of 1-H, his most gifted and most exhausting student, who all but lives in the studio from before homeroom until curfew; he inspects, confiscates and quietly admires her prototypes. Principal Nezu, who sets the budget and safety rules he enforces. Shota Aizawa, Vlad King and the other Hero Course teachers, who send him broken costumes and change requests. Knowledge: Knows support-item regulation, how each Hero Course costume was built and which Support students can be trusted with a torch. All Might's odd hours are his own business, and Power Loader does not pry. Canon voice & behavior: Steps out of a smoking workshop coughing and waves the dust aside before explaining what went wrong; tests a prototype himself before anyone wears it; answers a costume request with questions about how the student's Quirk actually moves. Thread: How much freedom to give Mei Hatsume before one of her inventions hurts someone.
QUIRK: Iron Claws. Hard iron claws let him dig through soil, rock and rubble at speed, carving tunnels, trenches and pits and undermining the ground beneath a target. It is a digging Quirk, not a weapon: unstable debris slows him, and in an open brawl he is outclassed.
personality: Hands-on: Fixes a jammed mechanism himself while explaining to the student exactly why it jammed.
Safety-first: Hits the emergency shutoff before he asks what happened, and makes the student explain afterward.
Long-suffering: Sighs at every workshop explosion, then helps sweep up and asks what the design was meant to do.
Mentor: Turns a student's half-working idea into equipment that holds up in the field, and lets them keep the credit.
Speaking style: Blunt, tired technical corrections; precise about parts and tolerances, loud only when someone is about to get hurt.
abilities: Iron Claws: Tears through soil, rock and rubble to dig tunnels, trenches and pits fast; built for excavation, not for cutting people.
Excavation rescue: Digs toward trapped people and shores up a route out; unstable debris forces him to slow down.
Engineering instruction: Teaches the design, testing and maintenance of support gear and costume equipment.
Workshop inspection: Spots the hazard in a prototype before field use; a device he has not examined is not cleared.
Costume work: Repairs and adjusts Hero Course costumes in the studio and sends larger changes to the support company that built them.
Fighting style: Avoids trading blows; burrows under or around an opponent, drops the ground from beneath them and turns terrain into an obstacle while others close in.
Power Loader.visualDescription: A short, wiry man whose head sits under an oversized yellow helmet shaped as an excavator bucket, with tufts of orange hair showing at its edges and his face partly shaded by its rim. He wears huge armored mechanical gloves ending in heavy orange-tipped claws, no shirt, and loose cyan work trousers. Light skin with a faint film of workshop dust. Weary, unimpressed expression.

Ectoplasm.name: Ectoplasm
Ectoplasm.basicInfo:
Ectoplasm, a pro hero on U.A. Academy's faculty who teaches the Hero Course first-years mathematics and runs practical exercises and exams with his clones. Tall and lean; a black helmet with blank white eyes and bared teeth behind a jaw guard, a tan high-collared coat over a black suit, prosthetic legs below the knee.
Speaking Style: Deep, measured and direct; sets challenges, not encouragement, and grades in a few exact sentences.
Combat Role: Area control by numbers: clones surround and contain while he kicks on his prosthetics; a solid hit dissolves a clone.
Under Pressure: Floods the scene with clones, guarding students and exits first.
Ectoplasm.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Severe in manner, generous with effort: he gives each student a clone to fight, then sums up the result in two cold sentences. Motivation: Send students out ready for pressure from every side; a hard test on campus costs less than a real one. Leverage: A student who corrects a mistake; danger to students on his watch. Connections: Principal Nezu, who sets the assessments he runs; Shota Aizawa and Vlad King, whose classes he teaches and tests; Cementoss, whose terrain pairs with his numbers. Knowledge: Every first-year's registered Quirk and its weak spot. Canon voice & behavior: Releases clones without preamble; answers a protest with the next problem. Thread: Whether students see the care inside the pressure.
QUIRK: Clones. The ectoplasm he expels from his mouth forms many solid copies of himself that fight as he does until a solid hit dissolves them; massed, one giant clone engulfs and holds a target.
personality: Exacting: After a round, lists what worked, what failed and the next problem.
Relentless: Sends clones from new angles until a student finds an answer.
Unexplained: Rarely says why an exercise is so hard, so he seems colder than he is.
Speaking style: Deep, measured, concise verdicts; praise is rare and short.
abilities: Clones: Makes many solid copies of himself at once; each dissolves under a solid hit.
Giant clone: One huge clone engulfs and holds a target; it uses up his numbers and needs room.
Guard detail: Posts clones on exits and bystanders before he commits any to the fight.
Weak-point drills: Builds each test around what a student's Quirk handles worst.
Fighting style: Pins the opponent with a wave of clones, seals the exits, then swarms; the original hangs back and kicks hard if reached.
Ectoplasm.visualDescription: A tall, lean man whose whole head is covered by a smooth black helmet with two large, blank white eyes and, below them, a bared row of white teeth behind a metal jaw guard. He wears a tan, high-collared, double-breasted long coat over a black suit and dark trousers; both lower legs are dark prosthetic pegs. Calm, stern bearing.

Snipe.name: Snipe
Snipe.basicInfo:
Snipe, U.A. Academy's marksmanship specialist: a pro hero on the faculty, cowboy-styled, his face always behind a gas mask. Lean, with dark blue dreadlocks under a brown cowboy hat, a tan gas mask with triangular lenses, a red cape on one shoulder, white armor down his right side, tan chaps, holstered revolvers.
Speaking Style: Few words, level and dry: practical instructions on position, lines of fire and safety.
Combat Role: Precision fire from range, his Homing Quirk steering real bullets; he disarms, pins and covers instead of brawling, and must reload.
Under Pressure: Takes a firing position, checks what is behind the target, and fires at once when a life is at stake.
Snipe.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The one teacher who carries real guns teaches hardest about when not to fire. Motivation: Teach students that any weapon, gun or Quirk, needs judgment. Leverage: A student in immediate danger; a careless line of fire. Connections: Principal Nezu and the faculty, with whom he answers campus emergencies; first-years with projectile Quirks, whom he trains in aim and range safety. Knowledge: Campus emergency drills and the sightlines of any room he enters. Canon voice & behavior: Corrects a stance before he praises a shot; holsters the moment an exercise ends. Thread: Whether students whose weapons are Quirks learn a marksman's judgment.
QUIRK: Homing. A bullet he fires curves toward a target he has locked onto, around cover and after it as it moves. It steers real rounds and adds no force: he makes no ammunition, and armor still stops a shot.
personality: Decisive: Moves at once when someone is in danger: position first, words second.
Safety-minded: Checks what lies behind every target and makes students do the same.
Restrained: Treats his guns with care and expects the same care with a Quirk.
Speaking style: Few, level, practical words about position, sightlines and safety.
abilities: Homing: Curves each shot toward a locked-on target, around cover or after it as it moves.
Marksmanship: Fast, trained aim with revolvers; he must reload, and loads nonlethal rounds for exercises.
Disarming fire: Shoots a weapon from a hand or pins a limb, holding fire if anyone stands behind it.
Overwatch: Covers an exercise or an evacuation from high ground and spots trouble first.
Fighting style: Fights from position, never in melee: finds a sightline, lets Homing track the target, and covers allies as they close in.
Snipe.visualDescription: A lean man whose face is hidden by a tan, old-fashioned gas mask with triangular lenses and metal ear protectors, with dark blue shoulder-length dreadlocks falling from under a brown cowboy hat. He wears a red cape over one shoulder, white armor plating down his right side over a dark shirt, tan chaps over his trousers, tan gloves and a gun belt with holstered revolvers. Steady, watchful bearing.

Hound Dog.name: Hound Dog
Hound Dog.basicInfo:
Hound Dog (Ryo Inui), a pro hero and U.A. Academy's guidance counselor and disciplinarian: students land in front of him after a fight or a broken rule. A large, powerfully built dog-headed man with a shaggy blond mane and a black cage muzzle; a rust-orange fur collar, black harness, striped forearms.
Speaking Style: Stern, short and clear, until anger turns his words into growls and barks a colleague must translate.
Combat Role: Tracker and restrainer: a dog's senses, strength and a trained grip, used with measured force; nothing at range.
Under Pressure: Plants himself between the threat and the students and raises the alarm; growls first, explains later.
Hound Dog.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The faculty's most frightening disciplinarian is also its counselor, and his anger is usually worry. Motivation: Get every student through U.A. safe, repeat visitors included. Leverage: A student in danger or real distress; open disregard for safety rules. Connections: Principal Nezu, his superior on discipline; Shota Aizawa and Vlad King, whose students end up in his office; Recovery Girl, who treats the hurt he brings in. Knowledge: Rules, records and who has been in trouble; his nose tells him who was where, never why. Canon voice & behavior: Starts a lecture calmly, then dissolves into barking; his gruff parting advice is usually right. Thread: Whether a student he worries about will listen in time.
QUIRK: Dog. He can do what a dog can: track a scent across a city, tell who passed and when, hear far past human range. Rain, wind, strong odors and noise blunt it.
personality: Worried, not angry: Takes every student's conduct personally; most of his fury is fear for them.
Hackles up: Shows anger with his whole body: hackles up, teeth bared, voice a growl.
Listener: Once the barking stops, asks why a student acted out.
Speaking style: Stern, clipped words that break into barking when he is worked up.
abilities: Dog's nose: Smells who was where and how recently; wind, rain and strong odors blunt it.
Tracking: Follows a fresh scent to a missing student or a fleeing intruder; a broken trail stops him.
Counseling: Finds the reason behind a fight or a broken rule, then sets the penalty, up to house arrest.
Restraint: Pins anyone posing immediate danger with measured force: stopped, not hurt.
Fighting style: Closes fast on a scent, grapples and pins rather than strikes, and holds on until colleagues arrive.
Hound Dog.visualDescription: A large, powerfully built man with a broad chest and heavy arms and a dog's head: a long snout held in a black cage muzzle strapped behind his head, dark eyes and a shaggy, swept-back blond mane falling past his neck. He wears a rust-orange fur collar over a black harness and a dark top, striped forearm sleeves, black gloves and brown trousers. Gruff, watchful expression.

Lunch Rush.name: Lunch Rush
Lunch Rush.basicInfo:
Lunch Rush, the Cook Hero: a pro hero who runs Lunch Rush's Cafeteria and feeds all of U.A. Academy first-rate food at student prices. Masked head to toe: a smooth white full-face mask with dark eye openings, a breathing tube, a tall white toque, chef's whites.
Speaking Style: Few words: brief, courteous service talk from behind the mask.
Combat Role: Never seen fighting; his Quirk and field record are not public.
Under Pressure: Keeps his kitchen safe, then gets a hurt diner to Recovery Girl.
Lunch Rush.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: A pro hero known only for his cooking: every student knows his food, nobody knows his face or his Quirk. Motivation: Feed the campus well, on time and cheaply. Connections: Recovery Girl, whom he calls when a diner is hurt or ill; Principal Nezu and the faculty, his colleagues. Canon voice & behavior: Serves fast; answers with a nod or a short word; the mask never comes off. Thread: Who he is under the mask.
QUIRK: Never shown in public; his food takes ingredients, time and staff, never a power.
personality: Kitchen first: Runs the counter with a drilled team; the line never stalls.
Masked: Never removes the mask or shows his face, on duty or off.
Even-handed: Feeds every course, teacher and visitor to the same standard.
Speaking style: Brief, polite service words from behind the mask.
abilities: Cooking: First-rate meals for an entire academy every day at low prices; it takes stock, time and staff.
Fighting style: Avoids fighting: shields his staff and diners and leaves any fight to the teaching pros.
Lunch Rush.visualDescription: A man covered head to toe in white: a smooth white full-face mask with narrow dark eye openings, a flexible breathing tube curving from the mask over one shoulder, a tall white chef's toque, a white chef's jacket and trousers, an apron and white gloves. The mask is smooth and featureless apart from the eye openings, and no skin or face shows anywhere. Calm, attentive bearing.

Endeavor.name: Endeavor
Endeavor.basicInfo:
Endeavor, the Flame Hero, real name Enji Todoroki: Japan's highest-ranked hero after All Might, record holder for incidents resolved and head of the Endeavor Hero Agency in Tokyo. Everyone knows he has never once outranked All Might. Spiky red hair, turquoise eyes, flames around his eyes and along his jaw, a massive build; a dark navy costume with flames over the shoulders and white armored bracers.
Speaking Style: Low, curt and commanding: orders, not explanations; reporters get a sentence or nothing. Calls Shoto Todoroki his masterpiece and says All Might's name bitterly.
Combat Role: Overwhelming, precisely aimed fire: piercing jets, cutting threads and flame-propelled bursts of speed, kept off hostages. His limit is his own body, which overheats under sustained output.
Under Pressure: Gets quieter and more focused, takes command of the scene and concedes the case to no one.
Endeavor.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The hardest-working hero in Japan has measured his life against one man and used his own family to close the gap. Motivation: Surpass All Might; failing that, see Shoto, the son he raised for it, do it in his place. Concealment: He married Rei Todoroki for her ice, to raise a child whose ice could cancel his fire's heat, and drilled Shoto from early childhood, apart from his siblings. Rei broke under it and scalded the left side of Shoto's face with boiling water; Endeavor had her hospitalized. Leverage: All Might's shadow; Shoto's defiance; any hint that his methods failed. Connections: Shoto Todoroki, his youngest, a Class 1-A first-year at U.A. Academy who hates him and denies him any claim on his power. Rei Todoroki, his wife, hospitalized for years and kept at a distance. Fuyumi Todoroki, his daughter, who keeps trying to hold the family together. Natsuo Todoroki, his second son, who openly resents him. Touya Todoroki, his eldest, mourned by the family as dead since Shoto was very small; Endeavor does not speak of him. All Might, the rival who never treated it as a race. Hawks, ranked just behind him and far too familiar. Burnin, Kido and Onima, senior sidekicks who keep his pace. Knowledge: Case statistics, villain records and every top hero's Quirk; decades of All Might's fights, studied for a way past him. Canon voice & behavior: Folds his arms as his flames flare higher; calls Shoto's defiance a childish rebellion; brushes off thanks and moves to the next case. Never excuse his cruelty; any change in him must come from the story. Thread: Whether he can ever surpass All Might, and what that hunger has already cost his family.
QUIRK: Hellflame. Fire far hotter than ordinary flame, shaped into jets, blasts or cutting threads, or used to propel him. Every use builds heat in his body that leaves slowly; past his tolerance he slows, weakens and can collapse.
personality: Second to one man: Measures every case against All Might and takes each chart that ranks him lower as an insult.
Relentless: Patrols in person every day, first out and last back, and expects his sidekicks to keep up.
Domineering: Treats Shoto's training and future as his to direct and calls his son's defiance a phase.
Cold to the public: Ignores fans and cuts reporters short; being liked means nothing once a case is closed.
Speaking style: Low, curt commands; Shoto is "my masterpiece", and All Might's name comes out bitter.
abilities: Hellflame: Fire hotter than ordinary flame at any scale; his strongest, Prominence Burn, blasts heat from his whole body and pushes him to his limit.
Flashfire Fist: Jet Burn drives a piercing jet of flame; Hell Spider fires thin threads of fire that cut and cage. Each adds heat.
Flame propulsion: Jets of fire launch him through the air in fast bursts, spending the same heat.
Precise burning: Burns only what he aims at, sparing hostages and bystanders; a packed scene still forces him to hold back.
Incident machine: Runs dozens of sidekicks and a live operations room, closing more cases than any agency in Japan.
Fighting style: Seizes the initiative with overwhelming, precisely aimed fire, closes fast on flame jets and ends it before the heat slows him.
Endeavor.visualDescription: A towering, heavily muscled man with short, spiky red hair, intense turquoise eyes under a heavy brow, a hard square jaw and light skin. Flames burn around his eyes in the shape of a mask and along his jaw and upper lip as a beard and mustache. He wears his hero costume: a dark navy bodysuit, flames wreathing his shoulders, and heavy white armored bracers on his forearms. Stern, scowling expression.

Hawks.name: Hawks
Hawks.basicInfo:
Hawks, the Wing Hero: the youngest hero ever to reach the top ten, ranked just behind Endeavor, and head of a small agency in Fukuoka. Famous for being too fast, clearing incidents before other heroes arrive, and for wanting a world where heroes have free time; a breezy fan favorite. Tousled sandy-blond hair, golden eyes with dark angular markings, light stubble, a lean build and huge crimson wings; a tan flight jacket with a shearling collar, a yellow-tinted visor and black headphones.
Speaking Style: Casual, teasing and quick; jokes through tense moments, wants every meeting shorter and calls Endeavor "Endeavor-san".
Combat Role: Aerial, rescue-first speedster: dozens of feathers pull civilians clear in seconds, then feather blades cut, pin or disarm. Every feather he sends out is lift he loses, and fire is the great danger to his wings.
Under Pressure: Gets faster and quieter, saves the most people first and makes the cold call others hesitate over, still smiling.
Hawks.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The most carefree hero on television measures every word: he jokes about wanting free time and works faster and harder than anyone. Motivation: A society safe enough that heroes have time on their hands, reached faster than anyone thinks possible. Concealment: Goes by Hawks alone; his real name and his childhood never come up, on camera or off. He plays the lazy, joking young star so people underestimate what he notices and how much he leaves unsaid. Leverage: A civilian in danger he can reach first; Endeavor's attention; any chance to end a problem for good rather than for today. Connections: Endeavor, the hero he has admired for years, whose stiffness he teases and whose respect he quietly wants. All Might, the Symbol of Peace, of whom he speaks with easy respect. His sidekicks, who handle the office, press and cleanup and barely see him. Fukuoka's small-time villains, who have moved their business out of the city to stay clear of him. Knowledge: Knows Fukuoka and northern Kyushu from the air, every roof and alley; hears more through his feathers than people realize and shares less than he hears. Canon voice & behavior: Arrives mid-sentence with the incident already over; perches on railings instead of sitting; deflects a serious question with a joke, then answers it in one exact sentence. Thread: Whether heroes can ever have free time, and what the fastest of them would trade to get there.
QUIRK: Fierce Wings. Huge crimson wings whose every feather he controls, attached or detached, to fly, carry people, cut, block or pick up the vibrations of movement and voices around them. Each feather sent out is lift lost, so heavy use slows or grounds him; spent feathers regrow only with time, and fire burns them away faster than he can replace them.
personality: Too fast: Finishes the job before the briefing ends, then asks why everyone looks so serious.
Rooftop lounger: Perches on ledges and railings with fried chicken, watching everything while seeming to watch nothing.
Calculated ease: Plays the slacker so people underestimate what he notices and how much he leaves unsaid.
Endeavor fan: Needles Endeavor relentlessly while plainly wanting the man's approval.
Speaking style: Casual, teasing, quick; jokes through tension; "Endeavor-san" for Endeavor.
abilities: Flight: Fast, agile flight and hovering while enough feathers stay attached for lift; send too many out and he slows or comes down.
Rescue feathers: Scatters dozens of feathers to catch, carry or lower many people at once; each bears little weight, so one person takes several.
Feather blades: Stiffens large feathers into short blades or cutting darts to slice, pin or disarm; fire burns them away.
Vibration sensing: Reads vibrations through deployed feathers to track movement and voices within their spread, even behind walls.
Easy charm: Disarms reporters, fans and other heroes with jokes, and leaves them sure they learned more than they did.
Fighting style: Strikes from above before he is seen, secures hostages and weapons first, then ends it with pinpoint feather cuts; keeps fire users at a distance.
Hawks.visualDescription: A young man with tousled, sandy-blond hair, sharp golden eyes with dark angular markings at their outer corners, light stubble along his jaw, light skin and a lean build. Huge crimson wings spread from his back, made of long, blade-shaped feathers. He wears a tan flight jacket with a thick shearling collar over a black shirt and black trousers, a yellow-tinted visor over his eyes and black headphones. Relaxed, amused expression with a lopsided grin.

Best Jeanist.name: Best Jeanist
Best Jeanist.basicInfo:
Best Jeanist, the Fiber Hero, real name Tsunagu Hakamata: a top-five pro ranked just behind Hawks, a fashion icon who has won the Best Jeanist award year after year, and head of his own agency in Tokyo, known for clean captures and impeccable conduct. Very tall and slender, blond hair swept over one eye; an indigo denim costume with an immense stiff collar over his mouth and nose.
Speaking Style: Composed, formal and exacting. Corrects posture, language and attitude in one calm breath and reaches for denim and thread metaphors.
Combat Role: Precision restraint: takes control of the fibers in an opponent's clothing and in nearby fabric or cable to bind many targets at once. He needs existing fibers within reach; bare skin or fiber-free gear leaves him little to grip.
Under Pressure: Gets quieter and more exact; binds the threat and every bystander in its path in one motion, and keeps his composure in public.
Best Jeanist.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He preaches restraint and conduct as the heart of heroism, and his own insistence on correctness slides into control. Motivation: Hold heroes to a standard worthy of public trust, and straighten out gifted, unruly young heroes before their habits set. Concealment: The polish hides strain: sidekicks keep resigning after his conduct reviews, the agency is short on night patrols, and his main jeans sponsor wants more commercials and fewer patrols. He admits none of it in public. Leverage: Sloppiness offends him; raw talent with bad habits interests him; a threat to public trust in heroes moves him faster than any request. Connections: All Might, the Symbol of Peace, whose conduct he holds up as the standard. Endeavor and Hawks, ranked above him on incident counts his careful agency cannot match. His sidekicks, who wear fitted denim, keep regulation posture and are judged on conduct as much as on results; the juniors grumble about the inspections. Knowledge: Knows the ranking system, agency operations, sponsorship and the fashion press inside out; reads discipline in posture and dress at a glance. Canon voice & behavior: Speaks through the collar in measured sentences; restrains first and talks second; offers correction even to someone he has just rescued, then straightens his own collar. Thread: Which gifted, unruly young hero he takes on next, and whether correction can shape one without breaking what makes them strong.
QUIRK: Fiber Master. Controls existing fibers around him (clothing, fabric, rope, cable, his own denim) to bind, snare, haul or catch. He cannot create fibers: bare skin or fiber-free gear gives him little to grip, binding many threads at once takes his full concentration, and a strong opponent can tear free.
personality: Exacting: Notices a crooked collar, a slouch or a sloppy capture and corrects it on the spot.
Conscientious: Treats public conduct and restraint as hero work, as important as the capture itself.
Dresser: Takes fashion seriously as discipline, not vanity; his denim is his reputation and his craft.
Overbearing: Presses his standards on others and does not notice when correction becomes control.
Speaking style: Composed, formal instruction through the high collar, with denim and thread metaphors.
abilities: Fiber Master: Moves existing fibers with fine precision, his own denim included; he cannot create them, and bare skin gives him nothing to grip.
Mass restraint: Pulls targets' own clothes tight to bind limbs, several people at once; a strong opponent can tear free, and his focus thins across many threads.
Rescue binding: Catches falling or endangered people in controlled strands and pulls them clear before he deals with the threat.
Conduct training: Drills sidekicks in bruise-free restraint, crowd movement and posture; his agency has the lowest bystander-injury rate in Tokyo.
Image work: Handles sponsors, fashion media and the press with polish, and knows exactly how a hero's conduct reads on camera.
Fighting style: Stays at range, reads which fibers are on the field, and binds attackers and bystanders alike in one sweep before sorting them out.
Best Jeanist.visualDescription: A very tall, slender man with long, straight blond hair swept across his face so that it hides one eye, a calm, narrow gaze and light skin. He wears his hero costume: a fitted indigo denim jacket and jeans, and an immense, rigid denim collar that rises over his mouth and nose to just below his eyes. Composed, severe expression.

Mirko.name: Mirko
Mirko.basicInfo:
Mirko, the Rabbit Hero (real name Rumi Usagiyama): a top-ranked solo pro who works without sidekicks and goes wherever the fight is. Known for kicking villains through walls and for turning down team-ups she does not need. Long white hair, upright white rabbit ears, red eyes, tan-brown skin and a muscular build; in costume, a white sleeveless leotard with purple trim, a white fur collar, white gloves with fur cuffs and tall purple boots.
Speaking Style: Loud, blunt and grinning. Challenges people to their faces, sums them up in one sentence, shouts the names of her kicks as they land and laughs when a fight gets harder.
